Let's introduce the new variable $u=4e^{x}+3.$ Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=4e^{x}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \mathrm{d}u=4e^{x}\,\mathrm{d}x.
$$

Next, we determine the new limits of integration:

| $x$ | $\ln(3)$ | $\ln(5)$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $15$ | $23$ |

Therefore, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_{\ln(3)}^{\ln(5)}\frac{20e^{x}}{4e^{x}+3}\,\mathrm{d}x &= \int_{\ln(3)}^{\ln(5)}\frac{5}{4e^{x}+3}\cdot 4e^{x}\,\mathrm{d}x \\ & = \int_{15}^{23}\frac{5}{u}\,\mathrm{d}u \\ & = 5\int_{15}^{23}\frac{1}{u}\,\mathrm{d}u \\ & = 5\ln|u|\big|_{15}^{23} \\ & = 5(\ln(23)-\ln(15)) \\ & = 5 \ln{\left(\frac{23}{15} \right)}.\end{aligned}
$$
